newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani court extends Bhutto husband's custody.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani court extends Bhutto husband's custody.

text.p: A Pakistani court on Saturday remanded ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari in custody for two weeks more, his lawyer said.

The authorities are holding Zardari, investment minister in his wife's cabinet, for alleged involvement in the death of Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza in September in a police shootout. Zardari denies the charge.
"The court has extended Zardari's jail custody up to January 18," defence lawyer Farooq Naik told Reuters.
He said the court had ordered police to submit the final charge-sheet against Zardari by January 18 or an interim complaint would be taken as final.

Zardari was first detained under a catch-all Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance on November 5 when President Farooq Leghari dismissed Bhutto's three-year-old government on disputed charges of corruption and maladministration.
When a court ordered his release on December 19, he was immediately re-arrested in the murder case.
Murtaza, Bhutto's younger brother, was a bitter critic of his sister's government.

His Lebanese-born widow Ghinwa, now chief of a breakaway faction of Benazir's Pakistan People's Party, has also accused former interior minister Naseerullah Babar, former Sindh province chief minister Abdullah Shah and police of plotting the murder of her husband. They all deny the charge.
Zardari's father, Hakim Ali Zardari, was also arrested on the New Year day in connection with an alleged land scam. He was remanded in custody on Saturday until January 11, Naik said.
